conversation.content: Please start a deployment setup for the checkout service.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload", "value": {"name": "checkout-service"}}]
Set it up to run three instances for normal traffic.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload/replicas", "value": 3}]
Give each running instance a modest CPU reservation of half a core.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload/resources/requests/perPodCpuCores", "value": 0.5}]
Also reserve 768 MiB of memory for each instance.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload/resources/requests/perPodMemoryMiB", "value": 768}]
Include the overall CPU reservation for the service and show the calculation behind it.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload/resources/requests/totalCpu", "value": {"cores": 1.5, "formula": "replicas * perPodCpuCores = 3 * 0.5"}}]
Add the overall memory reservation for the service and include the calculation used.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload/resources/requests/totalMemory", "value": {"MiB": 2304, "formula": "replicas * perPodMemoryMiB = 3 * 768"}}]
Add a short capacity note that reflects how many instances are expected to serve traffic, and include how it was determined.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload/capacitySummary", "value": {"servingReplicas": 3, "formula": "servingReplicas = replicas = 3"}}]
Make sure routine maintenance still leaves all but one instance available, and show the calculation.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload/availability/disruptionBudget/minAvailable", "value": {"pods": 2, "formula": "replicas - 1 = 3 - 1"}}]
Also allow only one instance to be taken down at a time, with the reasoning included.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload/availability/disruptionBudget/maxUnavailable", "value": {"pods": 1, "formula": "replicas - minAvailable = 3 - 2"}}]
Use the stable checkout container image from our registry and have it pulled only when needed.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload/image", "value": {"repository": "registry.example.com/apps/checkout-service", "tag": "1.8.2", "pullPolicy": "IfNotPresent"}}]
Run it in the production namespace and label it for the storefront app.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload/metadata", "value": {"namespace": "production", "labels": {"app": "storefront", "tier": "backend"}}}]
Have the container listen for HTTP traffic on port 8080 over TCP.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload/ports", "value": [{"name": "http", "containerPort": 8080, "protocol": "TCP"}]}]
Add a basic health check that hits the service over HTTP every ten seconds.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload/healthChecks/liveness", "value": {"path": "/healthz", "port": 8080, "periodSeconds": 10}}]
Add a readiness check for the main checkout endpoint with a short initial wait.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload/healthChecks/readiness", "value": {"path": "/ready", "port": 8080, "initialDelaySeconds": 15}}]
Set the runtime logging to use the info level.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload/env", "value": [{"name": "LOG_LEVEL", "value": "info"}]}]
Lock down the container so it runs without root privileges and cannot escalate permissions.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload/security", "value": {"runAsNonRoot": true, "readOnlyRootFilesystem": true, "allowPrivilegeEscalation": false}}]
Use rolling updates and keep a modest rollback history with a ten-minute rollout deadline.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload/rollout", "value": {"strategy": "RollingUpdate", "revisionHistoryLimit": 5, "progressDeadlineSeconds": 600}}]
Expose the service inside the cluster on the standard web port and route it to the container port already in use.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload/service", "value": {"type": "ClusterIP", "port": 80, "targetPort": 8080}}]
Make it reachable through the public checkout host using TLS.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload/ingress", "value": {"host": "checkout.example.com", "tlsSecret": "checkout-tls", "path": "/"}}]
Have Prometheus scrape this service for metrics on its usual endpoint.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload/monitoring", "value": {"prometheusScrape": true, "metricsPath": "/metrics", "metricsPort": 8080}}]
Place it on the general-purpose worker pool with the standard priority class.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload/scheduling", "value": {"nodePool": "general-purpose", "priorityClass": "standard"}}]
Add the owning team and their on-call contact so people know who to reach.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/workload/ownership", "value": {"team": "payments-platform", "onCall": "payments-platform-primary"}}]

edit_instruction: Please update the deployment to run 5 instances.
conversation_pattern: Center the artifact on a deployment with a replica count, per-pod CPU and memory requests, and availability settings, where EVERY derived field carries its own explicit formula written in the artifact: total CPU = replicas * perPodCpu, total memory = replicas * perPodMem, capacity summary = replicas, and each disruption-budget value has a stated formula (e.g. minAvailable = replicas - 1, maxUnavailable = 1). Do not include any availability field whose dependence on the replica count is not given by a stated formula. Around this core, add the realistic, independent details a deployment config would carry that do not depend on the replica count, and vary their number from sample to sample.
edit_pattern: Change the replica count to a specific new number.
cascade_pattern: Editing the replica count re-derives total CPU, total memory, capacity summary, and each disruption-budget value strictly from its stated per-pod value and formula. Per-pod requests and unrelated deployment fields stay unchanged.
annotation_notes: replicas 3->5; totalCpu=5*0.5=2.5, totalMem=5*768=3840, capacity=5, minAvailable=5-1=4, maxUnavailable=replicas-minAvailable=5-4=1. formula-text optional. | REVIEW EDIT (with author): removed no-op /workload/availability/disruptionBudget/maxUnavailable/pods (1->1: maxUnavailable=replicas-minAvailable=5-4=1 equals the current value, so the pods value does not change). It produced a phantom miss for a perfect model. The maxUnavailable formula text op (optional) stays.
